questions.question: Explain why mixtures can be separated by physical means. Describe, in order, how you would separate a mixture of sand, salt and iron filings, naming the property used at each step.
questions.expected_answer: The substances in a mixture are not chemically joined and keep their own properties, so they can be separated using differences in physical properties. Step 1: magnetic separation removes the iron filings (magnetism). Step 2: add water and stir; the salt dissolves, the sand does not (solubility). Step 3: filter; the sand remains as the residue and the salt solution passes through as the filtrate (particle size). Step 4: evaporate or crystallise the filtrate to recover the salt (water has a much lower boiling point than salt).

questions.question: Describe how pure water is obtained from salt water by distillation, naming the parts of the apparatus and explaining why filtration would not work. Explain how fractional distillation separates ethanol from water.
questions.expected_answer: The salt water is heated in a flask until it boils; the water vapour passes into a condenser, a tube surrounded by a jacket of cold running water, where it cools and condenses; the pure liquid water (distillate) drips into a collecting flask; the salt stays behind in the flask. A thermometer at the condenser opening reads 100 °C for water vapour. Filtration would not work because dissolved salt particles pass through filter paper. Fractional distillation: ethanol boils at 78 °C and water at 100 °C; when heated, ethanol vaporises first, rises through a fractionating column and is condensed and collected separately before the water.

questions.question: Describe the steps used to purify river water for drinking and state the purpose of each. Give one example each of separation used in mining and in medicine.
questions.expected_answer: Screening removes large objects such as sticks, leaves and litter. A chemical makes fine mud particles clump into flakes that settle (sedimentation), and the clearer water is decanted. Filtration through sand beds removes remaining fine particles. Chlorination kills micro-organisms that are too small to filter out. Mining: gold panning uses gold's high density; diamonds stick to grease tables because they repel water; magnets separate magnetic ores. Medicine: a centrifuge separates denser blood cells from lighter plasma.
